name: Engine R4: runtime on one WebGLRenderer, MotionPlayer, lab page and e2e
description: Wires schema, textures, 2D nodes, three layers, effects (isolated, three, stage), presets and tweens into MotionRuntime on a single Three WebGLRenderer, wraps it in <MotionPlayer>, adds /motion-lab.html and a Playwright spec (npm run engine:e2e) that checks every fixture for readiness, determinism, motion, colour and transparency. No Pixi.

readFirst: engine/src/core, schema, timeline, stage2d, three, effects index files (from M1, M2, R1, R2, R3)
web/src/player/PlayerBridge.tsx (the handle to mirror) and web/src/dev/three-check.tsx (hashCanvas)
engine/lab/stage-smoke.tsx and three-smoke.tsx (renderer settings) and playwright.config.ts (web server block)
extraGuardrails: Three.js only: no import of pixi.js, pixi-filters, @pixi/* or @react-three/* (lint enforces it).
The package.json edit is limited to making sure the script "engine:e2e": "playwright test -c engine/playwright.config.ts" exists.
manualGates: MG-1: owner opens http://localhost:5173/motion-lab.html, plays every fixture end to end, edits a tween in the JSON box and sees it apply, and records anything that looks wrong.

stories.title: assemble(): stage, nodes, isolation, presets and tweens on one clock
stories.description: As an engine developer, I want the whole build pipeline in one function that runs without WebGL so that wiring bugs are caught by unit tests.
steps: Read engine/docs/06-runtime-player.md section 'assemble' (steps 1 to 7).

Create engine/src/runtime/assemble.ts implementing steps 1 to 7: stage Scene and createStageCamera, nodes via createNode with factories.three, displays added in order, renderOrder by depth-first index on every mesh, isolateNode for 2D nodes with enabled effects, validateTargets warnings, MotionClock, expandPresets plus layer tweens compiled with a resolve that sends effect:<id> to the isolation or the three node and everything else to node.resolveTarget, buildStageChain, primeTimeline.
Return { stage, camera, nodes, clock, renderAt, warnings, destroy } (renderAt is completed in US-002; for now it may only set visibility).
Create engine/src/runtime/assemble.test.ts with renderer null, the chain test factory, a shapes-only doc and a doc with a fake three factory.
acceptance: assemble on a doc with two shapes and a group with one child returns 4 nodes, the stage has 3 children in layer order, and the second shape's meshes have a higher renderOrder than the first's
A shape with enter fadeIn has node.alpha.value 0 at its start and its base alpha after the preset duration (via clock.seek)
A text or shape layer with a glow effect is isolated (its display contains a plane, not its content), and a tween on effect:g reaches the fake chain's ref
A tween with an unknown property becomes one warning containing the layer id; destroy() destroys every node and the clock (spied)

stories.title: renderAt(t): visibility, opacity, node and isolation updates, stage render
stories.description: As an engine developer, I want each clock update to show exactly the layers that are on, fade groups correctly and render once so that every frame is a function of time.
steps: Read engine/docs/06-runtime-player.md (renderAt) and engine/src/stage2d/opacity.ts.

Complete renderAt(t): display.visible = isVisible for every node; applyOpacityTree on the root nodes; for visible nodes node.update?.(t, frame) and the isolation's update; then stageChain ? stageChain.render(renderer) : renderer.render(stage, camera); skip rendering when renderer is null.
Add tests to assemble.test.ts with a fake renderer object (render and setRenderTarget spies) passed as renderer and the chain test factory.
acceptance: A layer from 1 to 2 is invisible at seek 0.5, visible at 1.5 and invisible at 2
A fake three node from 0 to 3 gets update(1, 30) on seek(1) and no update on seek(4)
Each seek renders exactly once: renderer.render is called once per seek when there are no stage effects, and the stage chain's render once when there are

stories.title: MotionRuntime: WebGLRenderer, load, play, seek, whenReady, renderFrame, readPixel
stories.description: As a page author, I want one object that owns the canvas and the renderer and plays a doc so that pages and the player component stay thin.
steps: Read engine/docs/06-runtime-player.md section 'MotionRuntime' (renderer settings, load steps, whenReady, destroy).

Create engine/src/runtime/MotionRuntime.ts as specified, with the WebGLRenderer created through an injectable factory (for tests) and the settings from the doc; load parses, keeps the previous doc on failure, destroys the previous assembly, loads textures and three assets, assembles; readPixel reads the canvas (WebGL readPixels with y flipped to doc coordinates).
Create engine/src/runtime/index.ts and engine/src/runtime/MotionRuntime.test.ts with a fake renderer factory.
acceptance: load of an invalid doc returns ok false with errors and keeps the previous clock
whenReady(0.05) resolves false when a node's ready never settles and true when all settle (fake timers)
The renderer is created with preserveDrawingBuffer true, pixel ratio 1, outputColorSpace SRGBColorSpace and toneMapping NoToneMapping (checked on the fake)
destroy() disposes the assembly and calls renderer.dispose() and forceContextLoss()

stories.title: <MotionPlayer> component and MotionHandle
stories.description: As a React author, I want a drop-in player with controls and a handle like the director's PlayerHandle so that a later swap is mechanical.
steps: Read engine/docs/06-runtime-player.md section '<MotionPlayer>' and web/src/player/PlayerBridge.tsx and web/src/player/Player.tsx (controls).

Create engine/src/react/MotionPlayer.tsx: runtime created in an effect (StrictMode safe), load on doc change, doc and layer errors through props, MotionHandle via useImperativeHandle, controls (play/pause, seek range with step 1/fps, time, frame back and forward) unless controls is false, onTime once per animation frame while playing.
Create engine/src/react/index.ts and engine/src/react/MotionPlayer.test.tsx with vi.mock('../runtime/MotionRuntime') and @testing-library/react.
acceptance: Mounting and unmounting under StrictMode destroys every runtime it created (fake runtime counts)
Changing the doc prop calls load once with the new doc; an invalid doc calls onDocErrors with the errors
Clicking frame-forward at 30 fps seeks to the current time + 1/30; handle.seek(2) calls runtime.seek(2)

stories.title: Lab page /motion-lab.html with JSON editing and test hooks; public index
stories.description: As a project owner, I want a page to pick a fixture, edit its JSON live and see it play so that I can author and debug docs by hand.
steps: Read engine/docs/06-runtime-player.md section 'Lab page' and engine/lab/stage-smoke.tsx (hash, pixel readout).

Create engine/lab/motion-lab.tsx: fixture picker from import.meta.glob('../fixtures/*.json', { eager: true }), JSON textarea with a 400 ms debounce, schema errors with paths (last good doc keeps playing), MotionPlayer, layer errors, hash readout, ?doc=<name>&t=<sec>, and window.__motion { handle, ready, hash, pixel, errors } exactly as specified.
Create the stubs web/motion-lab.html and web/src/dev/motion-lab.tsx (one line importing ../../../engine/lab/motion-lab) following the existing stub pattern.
Create engine/src/index.ts as the public entry (schema, core, timeline, runtime, react public APIs).
Open http://localhost:5173/motion-lab.html and check every fixture plays; save a screenshot per fixture to debug/engine/.
acceptance: Every fixture in engine/fixtures loads with no schema errors, no layer errors and no console errors
Changing a tween's 'to' value in the textarea updates the picture after the debounce without a reload; invalid JSON shows an error and keeps the last good doc
window.__motion.ready() resolves true and window.__motion.hash() returns a 12-character hex string

stories.title: Playwright e2e: readiness, determinism, motion, colour and transparency
stories.description: As a project owner, I want an automated browser check of every fixture so that a regression anywhere in the engine shows up as a red test.
steps: Read engine/docs/06-runtime-player.md section 'End-to-end' and playwright.config.ts (copy its web server block; the engine needs no API server).

Create engine/playwright.config.ts: testDir 'e2e', workers 1, chromium, outputDir '../test-results', one webServer `npx vite --config web/vite.config.ts` with DIRECTOR_WEB_PORT 5290, port 5290, reuseExistingServer false, baseURL http://localhost:5290; make sure package.json has the engine:e2e script.

Create engine/e2e/motion-lab.spec.ts: for each fixture (listed with node:fs) steps 1 to 4 of the doc; plus the basic-2d colour check ((255, 0, 0) ± 1 at the red shape's centre) and the three-postfx transparency check (a corner of the hero layer equals the plate colour ± 2).
Run `npm run engine:e2e`; fix failures in engine/ (any earlier engine code may be fixed; say so in notes).
acceptance: `npm run engine:e2e` passes for every fixture in engine/fixtures
For each fixture the spec asserts equal hashes for two seeks to 40 % and a different hash at 80 %
The colour check and the transparency check are in the spec and pass; screenshots exist in debug/engine/ for every fixture
